code: // Create once on a permitted miss.

overview.explanation: The solid arrows show the miss path. The cache block returns directly on a hit, and the permission block throws directly on denial. The RealHours owner is created only if absent. invalidate clears cached_, sending the next permitted call back through the miss path; it leaves real_ intact.

focus.title: Protect every path to a result
focus.what: The proxy rejects denied access before returning even a remembered value.
focus.where: This block is the first part of opening.
focus.why: A fast cache path must not bypass the permission contract.
focus.invariant: Every returned result follows a successful permission check.
focus.risk: Checking permission only on misses leaks cached data after revocation.
explain: The comment states the ordering rule.
Test whether access is currently denied.
Give the denial message and complete the throw.
Return the stored integer only if an optional value exists.

focus.title: Create once, fetch on misses
focus.what: A permitted miss creates the real service if needed, then stores a fetched result.
focus.where: This block runs only when permission succeeded and the cache was empty.
focus.why: Lazy construction avoids unused service objects, while caching avoids repeated reads.
focus.invariant: The cache is assigned only after the real call returns successfully.
focus.risk: Concurrent misses need synchronization; the current example is single-threaded.
explain: Check whether the real-service owner is empty.
Begin assigning a newly created owner.
Construct a RealHours object with make_unique.
Pass the borrowed source to its constructor.
Close the creation branch; an existing object is reused.
Fetch a value and engage the optional cache.
Close the miss path and opening method.
